minutes.headline: Board held a facilities workshop on the old primary school and Brooks House; no vote, and a reserve officer and interim inspector were appointed.
minutes.summary: After a short business meeting (two appointments, warrant dates, a bond anticipation note, warrants), the board held a workshop on town buildings with APDC and Historical Society members. The APDC's letter says the town is in violation of the demolition-by-neglect bylaw for the old primary school and may soon be for the Brooks House. The group discussed selling or leasing, a single-family reuse of the Brooks House, and a plan to seek Town Meeting funding for TC Passios drawings.

what_happened.line: The board held a workshop on town buildings with APDC and Historical Society members, covering the old primary school and Brooks House; no vote was taken.
The board will seek a Town Meeting article to fund detailed drawings of the TC Passios plan of record and will continue workshops with other groups.
The board approved an interim local building inspector; the appointment passed.
Votes to appoint a reserve police officer, set the Annual Town Meeting warrant dates and sign bond anticipation notes for the middle high school were not audible in the recording.
The warrant for the May 4, 2019 Annual Town Meeting was set to open Jan 15 and close March 21 at 6 p.m.; the outcome of that vote is not audible.

why_it_matters: The old primary school and Brooks House are town-owned buildings, and any decision to repair, sell, lease or demolish them would come to Town Meeting as a funding vote and affect the town budget, mostly taxes.

Repair costs for the old primary school were described as near the cost of demolition, and the debt discussion shows these projects would compete with other building needs such as TC Passios, so residents may be asked to vote on drawings funding in May.
